chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Auditions, novelty acts and the supper-club food
summary: No food; the club drew show people; other acts were comedians and novelty; she chose her own material.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: stayed one night. They had a way of auditioning performers in front of a live audience. I mean, in fact an act would come in and audition for a week. They'd try to see how the act would go over and if they went over well they made out a contract.
And would these all be singers?

No, they had comedians, all kinds of novelty acts, but strictly stand-up type acts because the stage was very small. But they had the Bill Baird Puppets in there, and his wife came in and they did the puppet show in there with their characters. The strange thing about it and the room was small, I don't know if the Ruban Bleu held over 150 people.

No, no food. There was no food. The only thing you could get there was Welsh Rabbit Salad because you see the Ruban Bleu was on the second floor in the building. I think it was the Barbizon Hotel. The building there now is Corning Glass. But there was a very popular restaurant down stairs, Theodores.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

That was where mostly all the show people came to eat. But they closed at 8:30. You see, they served dinner. They too were catering to the theater crowd and people went there to eat dinner and they would leave there an go to the theater. We got them when they came out of the theater and the few that didn't make the theater would come up-stairs. In fact, the act would go on first at the Rue Ban Bleu. It had very little audience, maybe two or three people. So the fourth act and the first act on the second-go-round would get the best crowd. Because we actually filled up after the theater let out. So I would say around ten or eleven o'clock we really got the crowd. Of course, during the way well, this was during the war, '42 and on up, we had allot of brass coming in. They discovered the Rue Ban Bleu. And then of course the ropes went up. We were always turning people away. It was always exclusive but it became more exclusive, not because it tried to be, it just became exclusive because it didn't have anyplace to put the people. But it was a wonderful engagement for me and I had the opportunity to work with a lot of different performers, different types of acts, and as I said before, it was a joy working
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And you got to choose your own material?
Oh, yes, yes. I did everything I wanted to do. Of course, 'Loch Lomond' remained the favorite. Invariably I had to do 'Loch Lomond' twice a night that I went on. But it was good. I really enjoyed it.
